A. Popularity baseline.description: Rank displayed eligible articles by training-period click count.

C. TF-IDF + Jaccard.description: Cosine-primary lexical and set similarity ablation.

D. TF-IDF + Jaccard + recency/popularity.description: Full weighted net score before diversity reranking.

E. Full model + diversity reranking.description: Model D followed by greedy cosine redundancy reranking.

F. Multi-interest profiles.description: Model D weights, but the history is split into leader-clustered interests: cosine against the best-matching interest and top-K slots shared in proportion to interest size.

aggregation: Macro-average query metrics within each user, then macro-average users.
candidate_policy: Only valid articles shown in each held-out impression; consumed history excluded.
history_copy_policy: Shown articles with the same normalized title as, or cosine >= 0.9 to, an already-read article are removed for every model, including the baseline.
history_policy: Each held-out impression's recorded pre-impression history only.
normalization: Cosine and Jaccard are divided by their maximum over each impression's candidates; then weighted mean: sum(weight_i * component_i) / sum(weight_i).
popularity_policy: Click counts from training impressions only.
recency_policy: MIND has no publication time. Proxy timestamp: first training impression that showed the article; training-log start for articles only seen in training histories; the cutoff for articles never seen before it (new).
split_method: global chronological cutoff; train timestamp <= cutoff; test timestamp > cutoff
tuning_policy: Fixed component weights specified before evaluation; no evaluation-set tuning.
